scene_translation: The man turned down a narrow alley behind the shrine, and Tesuto followed in silence, barely breathing. At the end of the alley stood a single rusted iron door, where the man stopped and looked back. "I thought you'd follow," he said quietly. There was not the slightest surprise in his voice — as if he had known all along it would come to this. He slowly pushed the door open and added, "If you want to talk about your grandmother, please come inside. It's quiet underground."
grammar_note: 【まるで〜かのようだった】 means 'it was as if / just like ~' — used to describe something that strongly resembles a hypothetical situation. まるで sets up the comparison, and かのようだ (or かのようだった in past) closes it. Example: まるでずっと前からこうなることを知っていたかのようだった — 'It was as if he had known all along it would come to this.' Note also the register of the man's speech: polite ます/です forms, but with an unsettling calm that makes the politeness feel more eerie than friendly.

mystery_memo: The grey-suited man has now revealed he knows the player's name and has some connection to the grandmother — he is not hostile but unsettlingly prepared. The rusted iron door almost certainly leads to the underground passages partially mapped in the notebook; this is the first physical intersection of the map clue and the story's movement. The coin locker key has not yet been used — the underground passage may contain another locker or locked box. The old bookshop owner's fear is likely linked to this man or whoever he works for; his silence is protective, not accidental.
